text: GraphQL Debugger. Pause, edit and read every GraphQL request.
Apollo’s Automatic Persisted Queries send a SHA-256 hash, not the query. The Network panel can’t show you what ran.
Tell GraphQL Debugger which requests to watch.
Press Start (Ctrl+E). The bar stays up whenever requests are being rewritten.
Each hash is swapped, the server asks for the full query, and Apollo retries. The row resolves in place.
Open any operation to read and copy the full query and its variables.
Copy as cURL to replay it from a terminal, with the headers captured from the page.
Set a breakpoint on an operation name. Matching requests pause before they are sent.
Edit the query, variables or headers, then resume. Only the request waits; the page keeps running.
Filter by name, URL or request type.
Load the schema by introspection, reusing the headers from live traffic.
Stop when you’re done. Nothing from your traffic leaves your browser.
GraphQL Debugger. Breakpoints, APQ and schema for GraphQL, in DevTools.
